info.title: AI Attendance Management System
info.description:
AI-powered attendance management using face recognition.

**Authentication:** call `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, then click the **Authorize** button above and paste the `access_token`.

post.description:
Exchange email and password for an access/refresh token pair.

The access token is short-lived and sent on every subsequent request as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The refresh token is long-lived and used
only against `/auth/refresh`.

Note the `responses=` argument above: it documents the failure cases in
the generated OpenAPI spec, so the interactive docs at /docs show clients
exactly what can go wrong. This is your API documentation requirement
being satisfied automatically rather than written by hand.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new token pair
post.description:
Obtain a fresh access token without re-entering credentials.

Returns a NEW refresh token as well -- the old one is revoked. See
AuthService.refresh_access_token for why rotation matters.

This endpoint is deliberately unauthenticated: the refresh token IS the
credential. Requiring a valid access token here would defeat the purpose,
since the whole reason to call it is that the access token has expired.

End the session by revoking its refresh token.

Requires BOTH a valid access token (proving who you are) and the refresh
token to revoke. Without the access token requirement, anyone holding a
stolen refresh token could... log you out. Minor, but there is no reason
to allow it.

post.summary: Revoke every active session for the current user
post.description: Log out of every device. Useful when a device is lost or stolen.

get.description:
Return the authenticated user.

The frontend calls this on page load to restore session state -- it holds
a token in storage but needs the user's name and role to render the right
dashboard.

No database call in the endpoint body: `get_current_user` already loaded
and validated the user. Note that `UserResponse` strips `password_hash`
even though the model carries it.

post.description:
Change the current user's password and terminate all sessions.

Every device must log in again, including this one -- deliberate, since a
password change is often a response to compromise.

Open a session for one offering.

Only one session may be open per offering at a time -- a second attempt
returns 409. Faculty may open sessions only for offerings they teach.

403.description: You do not teach this offering

post.summary: Close a session and auto-mark absentees
post.description:
Close the session.

Every enrolled student without a record is marked ABSENT in one bulk
insert -- absence is derived as a set difference, never observed.
Students who enrolled after this session's date are excluded.
Cancelled sessions are excluded from attendance percentages entirely.

Admin-only, audit-logged. Removes auto-generated absent records but
preserves any records a human marked by hand.

get.description:
Every enrolled student, marked or not.

Unmarked students appear with status=null, which is what lets the faculty
UI show "12 of 40 marked" and offer one-click manual marking without a
second request.

post.summary: Recognise faces in a frame AND write attendance
post.description:
The automatic marking endpoint. Called at ~2 fps by the faculty UI.

IDEMPOTENT: a student standing in frame for ten seconds generates twenty
calls; the first creates a record and the other nineteen are harmless
no-ops returning `already_marked: true`. That property is what makes a
continuous camera stream safe against this endpoint.

Recognition is restricted to students enrolled in this offering, which is
both faster and less prone to false positives.

post.summary: Mark or correct a student by hand
post.description:
The fallback that makes the system safe to deploy.

If the camera fails, if recognition misses someone, if a student's face
is not enrolled -- attendance still happens. The system assists faculty;
it never replaces their judgement.

put.description:
Override a record.

Corrections of face-marked records are your false-positive count -- the
accuracy metric for your project report. Every one is recorded with who
changed it and when.

post.description:
Pure recognition. Writes no attendance.

Deliberately separate from mark-face: an endpoint that mutates state
should always be distinguishable from one that does not. This one is safe
for testing, debugging, and future features (visitor identification, exam
hall verification) with no risk of touching attendance data.

post.description:
Manual index rebuild.

Normally automatic after enrolment. Exposed for the multi-worker case
where one process has a stale index -- the known limitation documented in
the deployment diagram.

get.description:
Per-subject breakdown plus an overall figure.

A student may view ONLY their own record -- horizontal privilege
escalation defence. Faculty and admin may view any.

`percentage` is null when no eligible sessions have occurred: no
percentage exists yet. The UI shows a dash, not 0%.

get.summary: Faculty-wise attendance across all their offerings
get.description: Class averages, session counts, and defaulter counts per offering.

Students at risk, with `shortfall_sessions` -- how many consecutive
future classes they must attend to climb back above the threshold.

That number is what students actually want to know, and it is more
actionable than a bare percentage.

schema.title: Response Defaulters Api V1 Offerings  Offering Id  Defaulters Get

get.summary: All analytics for one class in a single snapshot
get.description:
Everything the analytics page renders, in one request.

Bundled rather than split into five endpoints so the charts are guaranteed
to agree with each other. Five separate calls could interleave with a
session closing, leaving the daily chart including a session the student
percentages do not -- numbers that silently contradict each other on screen.

get.summary: Attendance per session over recent days
get.description:
One point per CLOSED session, not per calendar day.

Days with no class produce no point. Emitting zeros for weekends and
holidays would draw a sawtooth that reads as collapsing attendance when
in fact nothing happened.

schema.title: Response Daily Analytics Api V1 Analytics Offerings  Offering Id  Daily Get

get.description:
Monthly rate computed from summed totals, never averaged from daily rates.
Averaging percentages would weight a 5-student session equally with a
40-student one.

schema.title: Response Monthly Analytics Api V1 Analytics Offerings  Offering Id  Monthly Get

get.description:
ALL students, not only those below threshold -- a distribution built from
defaulters alone would show only the left tail.

schema.title: Response Student Percentages Api V1 Analytics Offerings  Offering Id  Students Get

get.description: Compare across the offerings one faculty member teaches.

schema.title: Response Subject Percentages Api V1 Analytics Faculty  Faculty Id  Subjects Get

get.description:
Ranked by ABSENCE COUNT, not percentage -- deliberately a different
question from the defaulter list.

A student at 50% who missed 1 of 2 classes is at risk. A student at 67%
who missed 15 of 45 is not turning up. The first is a threshold problem;
the second is a pastoral one.

schema.title: Response Top Absentees Api V1 Analytics Offerings  Offering Id  Absentees Get

get.description:
Unauthenticated health check.

Deployment tooling, load balancers, and uptime monitors call this to
decide whether the process is alive. It must never require authentication
-- a monitor holding credentials is a credential you have to rotate.

Deliberately returns no version or environment detail: this endpoint is
reachable by anyone, so it should disclose nothing.

AttendanceStatus.title: AttendanceStatus
AttendanceStatus.description:
The status recorded for one student in one session.

PRESENT  -- recognised by face, or manually marked present by faculty.
ABSENT   -- enrolled but not marked present when the session closed.
            Note this is *derived*, never observed: you cannot detect
            someone who is not there. It is computed as
            (enrolled students) minus (marked students) at session close.
LATE     -- present, but arrived after a configurable grace period.
            Counts toward attendance percentage.
EXCUSED  -- authorised absence (medical, official duty). Excluded from
            the percentage *denominator* so it neither helps nor hurts.

ChangePasswordRequest.title: ChangePasswordRequest
ChangePasswordRequest.description:
WHY THE CURRENT PASSWORD IS REQUIRED
------------------------------------
The user is already authenticated -- so why ask again?

Because an unattended logged-in session is a real threat. Someone walks up
to a faculty member's open laptop and changes the password: they now own
the account permanently, and the legitimate owner is locked out. Requiring
the current password means possessing the session is not sufficient.

This is standard practice on every serious platform, for exactly this
reason.

LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest
LoginRequest.description:
Credentials submitted to /auth/login.

EmailStr does real format validation (via email-validator), not a naive
regex. Invalid input is rejected by FastAPI with a 422 before your endpoint
function runs -- so the service layer can assume a syntactically valid
address and never has to re-check.

SubjectAttendance.title: SubjectAttendance
SubjectAttendance.description:
Attendance for one student in one offering.

`percentage` is None when no eligible sessions have occurred yet -- NOT
zero. Returning 0% would flag every student as a defaulter on day one.

TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse
TokenResponse.description:
Issued on successful login or refresh.

`token_type: "bearer"` follows RFC 6750. The client sends the access token
back as:  Authorization: Bearer <token>

`expires_in` is seconds, not a timestamp -- so the client does not need its
clock to agree with the server's. A well-built frontend uses it to refresh
proactively (say at 80% of lifetime) rather than waiting for a 401 and
retrying.

UserResponse.title: UserResponse
UserResponse.description:
Safe representation of a user.

Compare this field list against the `User` model. Absent here, present
there: password_hash, failed_login_count, locked_until.

That omission is the entire point of having a separate schema. It is not
an oversight -- it is the security boundary, made explicit and reviewable.

`from_attributes=True` lets Pydantic read from a SQLAlchemy object rather
than requiring a dict, so an endpoint can `return user` and Pydantic
extracts exactly these fields and no others.
